phase_evolution.value: The BCC and partially ordered B2-type phases were retained after spark plasma sintering along with the in-situ formation of the Fe5Si3-type silicide phase; γ-brass type survives only as a trace. Retention of BCC and B2 is attributed to strong Fe–Al and Ni–Al bonding and the sluggish diffusion effect in the high entropy steel; silicide formation results from undissolved Si remaining after milling and the strongly negative Fe–Si and Mn–Si binary mixing enthalpies.

interface_notes.value: SEM/BSE contrast classes: white = B2 (rich in Al and Ni), light grey = BCC (rich in Fe, Mn, Ni), dark grey/black = γ-brass type and Fe5Si3-type intermetallic; dark features show an onion-type layered appearance. Regions of γ-brass type are difficult to distinguish by EPMA due to its very low phase fraction.
